description: The top of the poster doubles as a timeline: each red dotted 'time' line is drawn parallel to the density lines because the universe's average density falls as it ages (rho ~ 3/(32 pi G t^2)). The tick ruler under the time labels is the DENSITY axis.
density_model: density_log10_kg_m3 is the mean density of a flat LambdaCDM universe (Planck 2018: H0 = 67.66, Omega_m = 0.3111, Omega_r = 9.15e-05), i.e. 3H^2/(8 pi G). hubble_diameter_log10_m = 2c/H at that time; the sphere of that diameter at that density sits exactly on the black-hole line. 'now' uses a = 1 exactly; the model age is 13.78 Gyr. friedmann_density_log10_kg_m3 is the radiation-only formula, which is wrong after ~50,000 years.

calibration.note: Top ruler 'DENSITY 10^n g/L'. Values taken as a uniform 9 decades per tall tick, anchored on the printed '3' (water). Only valid along the ruler row; density lines run diagonally.

density_lines.note: Unspecified on the chart; the line sits near 10^16-10^17 g/L (nuclear density is ~2.3e17 kg/m^3).

start.label: The Big Bang: all three walls meet
start.summary: 2.7e-44 s (half the Planck time) · 2 Planck lengths across · half the Planck mass
start.explanation: The Hubble sphere is exactly as small as quantum uncertainty allows and as dense as gravity allows, so the three walls cross at one point. Earlier than this they would cross over and the triangle turns inside out: that needs a theory of quantum gravity. Where exactly they meet depends on factor-of-2 conventions (diameter vs radius, hbar vs h); this chart's put it at half the Planck time.

history.description: The universe at 700 moments from the instant the three walls meet (half the Planck time) to today (flat LambdaCDM, Planck 2018). Sample spacing is even in log time after the Big Bang up to half the age of the universe, then even in log time before today. The last row is today exactly.
history.temperature_note: Radiation temperature. Before 1e9 s (~30 years) it is computed from the radiation density with the Standard Model's count of relativistic species g*(T) (106.75 above the top-quark mass, falling smoothly to 3.36 after electron-positron annihilation); afterwards it is T_cmb / a.
